label: prf:mi-sw-abelianisation-cartan
title: Proof that the Cartan component recovers the SW differential
html:
On the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_c \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) the principal \mathrm{SU}(2)-bundle P trivialises (every \mathrm{SU}(2)-bundle over S^2 is classified by \pi_1(\mathrm{SU}(2)) = 0). The connection \nabla_A therefore reduces to a \mathfrak{su}(2)-valued 1-form A|_{\mathcal{S}_c}. By the weight-space decomposition (weight space decomposition), the restriction splits as

  A\big|_{\mathcal{S}_c}
  = 
  A^0 \otimes H \;+\;
  A^+ \otimes E_+ \;+\;
  A^- \otimes E_-,

where H, E_\pm are the standard generators of \mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{C}) = \mathfrak{su}(2) \otimes_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbb{C} (the decomposition uses the complexified form). The Cartan component A^0 is a \mathrm{U}(1)-valued 1-form on \mathcal{S}_c. Since \mathcal{S}_c \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) the spectral curve (color bundles) restricts to a single sheet, and the Higgs-field eigenvalue is the color coordinate X. The abelian component therefore satisfies A^0 = X\, dz = \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}, recovering the Seiberg--Witten differential in the trivialising gauge; A^0 is gauge-dependent, so the identity is a statement in that gauge. \square
